report.narrative: The core concept of a collapsible bicycle helmet with honeycomb liner, overlapping cells, rigid locking when actuated, and flat collapse is heavily anticipated by WO2023233224A1 (Monopro Ltd) and the US12268268B2/US12740611 family. WO2023233224A1 discloses all elements except the quarter-turn twist actuation: honeycomb protective configuration, staggered lines of attachment, arcuate end plates engaging to form a rigid loop, collapsed flattened form, and impact absorption through progressive crumpling. The US12268268B2 family discloses radial honeycomb matrix with folded↔expanded transition and side frames. US11857020 (Coco Worldwide) discloses rotation between helmet components (crown rotates 180° relative to base) with locking means, but uses a different mechanism (pivot + toggle latch, not twist-lock). The only potentially novel element is the quarter-turn (90°) twist actuation of the shell relative to the liner. However, quarter-turn twist-lock mechanisms are ubiquitous in mechanical engineering (US4893978, US6575682, US9200660, US12736079, US20110110716A1, US4653970, US5123795 — dating from 1970s-2020s). Applying a known mechanical principle (quarter-turn fastener) to a known structure (folding helmet with rotating components per US11857020) would likely be rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The specific geometry of how the twist actuates the honeycomb cells (cam surfaces, detent positions) might be the only protectable aspect, but this would be a very narrow claim.

matrix.label: quarter-turn twist actuation
matrix.reads_on: Not found in helmet patents. Well-known in general mechanical engineering (US4893978, US6575682, US9200660, US12736079, US20110110716A1, US4653970, US5123795). US11857020 teaches 180° rotation between helmet components.

report.limitations: No patent found disclosing a quarter-turn (90°) twist of the shell relative to the liner to lock/unlock a honeycomb structure in a helmet. The specific cam/detent geometry of the twist actuation mechanism may be protectable as a narrow design patent or utility patent claim.
